## In the MRP

The parameter `Growth` measures the economy's expansion speed and its stability. It uses two symbols. The first is $\mu_r$, the real log-growth drift. It is the average of the logarithm of real gross domestic product growth over the last 25 years. The data comes from the International Monetary Fund World Economic Outlook. The second symbol is $\sigma$, the volatility of nominal growth. It is the standard deviation of nominal growth. Nominal growth is real growth plus realized inflation. Default risk depends on nominal shortfalls, so nominal volatility matters. The model does not filter out crisis years. Crisis years are information, not outliers. The nominal drift is $\mu$. It equals $\mu_r$ plus expected euro-area inflation plus the inflation differential. Lower drift or higher volatility reduces the country's borrowing capacity.

## In the DAP

Country teams assess `Growth` in task C1*. They look for four types of issues. First is C1-E, a broken or dominated sample. Red flags include a missing 25-year window, a regime change like euro accession, or a single year moving $\sigma$ by more than a quarter. Second is C1-T, a structural break in trend. Red flags include a medium-term forecast more than one percentage point from the historical mean for two vintages, or evidence from demographics, energy prices, or sectoral shifts. Third is C1-A1, growth not thin-tailed or serially independent. Red flags include negative skewness, shortfalls in runs, or exposure to rare disasters like energy dependence. Fourth is C1-A2, an inherited competitiveness gap. Red flags include a cumulative real appreciation of unit labour costs against the euro area above 10 log points, or a medium-term forecast not below the historical trend despite such a gap. Type-A issues never justify a higher drift or a lower $\sigma$.

## Methods by Document Type

### [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) uses historical gross domestic product data and medium-term forecasts to assess the `Growth` parameter. It notes that productivity growth can be uneven across sectors. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 11, p. 58" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 11, p. 58">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports real gross domestic product growth, nominal unit labour cost growth, and wage growth to assess economic momentum and competitiveness pressures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimates growth based on the Spring 2026 Forecast. The report highlights the importance of real gross domestic product growth in reducing the debt-to-gross domestic product ratio through the denominator effect. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimates potential growth based on production function approaches. It notes stagnant labour supply due to population ageing and lagging total factor productivity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The report uses historical GDP growth data and medium-term forecasts to assess growth potential. It highlights structural factors such as labor market rigidity and low business dynamism as constraints on productivity and growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 9-10" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 9-10">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission’s medium-term growth forecasts deviate from historical means, influenced by structural factors such as demographic trends, energy prices, and sectoral shifts in export markets. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast to project potential growth (0.5% average 2026-2030) and real GDP growth (0.6% in 2026, 0.9% in 2027). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses historical gross domestic product growth data (2023-2025 average of 2.1%) and medium-term forecasts (2026: 1.8%, 2027: 1.6%) to assess the growth trend. It compares the medium-term forecast to the historical mean to identify structural breaks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2-3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2-3">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses historical GDP growth data to illustrate productivity stagnation and regional disparities. It references Eurostat and [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) forecast data for medium-term trends. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 47" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 47">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides historical real GDP growth and medium-term forecasts from the Commission’s Spring 2026 Forecast. It notes productivity levels relative to the EU average. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission uses standard national accounts data for GDP. It also references Modified Gross National Income to better reflect the income standards of Irish residents, excluding globalization effects. The report notes that GDP figures are heavily influenced by multinational activity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimates real GDP growth based on contributions from private consumption, investment, and net exports. Potential growth is linked to productivity shifts towards higher value-added activities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 10" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 10">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides estimates for real GDP growth, nominal growth components, and detailed analysis of productivity trends using unit labor costs and total factor productivity. It uses 25-year historical data windows for some comparisons but focuses heavily on recent structural breaks in the financial sector. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 3, 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 3, 4">ⓘ</button>
- The report provides historical real GDP growth and medium-term forecasts based on the European Commission's Spring 2026 Forecast. It highlights structural factors affecting trend growth, such as demographic ageing and low investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides historical real GDP growth and medium-term forecasts, which are inputs for estimating the growth drift and volatility parameters. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimates potential growth and historical trends using standard macroeconomic models, noting structural constraints such as labor productivity gaps and aging demographics. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 50-51" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 50-51">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission uses macroeconomic forecasts based on demographic projections, energy-price regimes, and sectoral shifts to estimate medium-term growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides forecasts for real GDP growth, highlighting a slowdown in 2025-2026 driven by fiscal consolidation and external factors. The structural break in trend is evident in the deviation of the medium-term forecast from the historical mean. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd)

- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses its Economic Outlook database for short-term projections and its Long-Term Model for long-term scenarios. Potential GDP is estimated using structural methods. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 26" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 26">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses historical gross domestic product (GDP) growth data and potential growth estimates based on production function approaches, accounting for capital stock, labour force, and total factor productivity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that potential gross domestic product per capita growth has weakened since the pandemic, driven by a shrinking working-age population, low productivity growth, and high energy costs. Trend labour productivity growth is low, held back by low capital intensity and rising part-time employment. The medium-term growth forecast deviates significantly from the pre-crisis trend, reflecting permanent output loss from the 2022–2024 recession. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- The economy experienced a prolonged recession, its longest since 1945, triggered by energy price shocks. Growth shortfalls came in runs, with real GDP declining between Q4 2022 and Q3 2024. The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) highlights exposure to rare disasters, including energy dependence on imported fossil fuels and geopolitical risks affecting trade value chains. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- Unit labour costs rose significantly, eroding industrial competitiveness. Electricity prices for non-household consumers were substantially higher than in late 2021. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 71" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 71">ⓘ</button>
- Real gross domestic product growth is projected to moderate as the economy rebalances from consumption-led to investment-led growth. Labour productivity growth slowed since the pandemic. The manufacturing sector has seen negative average quarterly growth since 2023 due to higher energy prices and unit labour costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 20, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 20, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that even at current growth rates, convergence to average [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) income levels would take decades. Structural reforms (investment, skills, productivity) are estimated to raise per capita gross domestic product. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- Unit labour costs have tripled since European Union accession, surpassing cost growth in other European Union competitor countries. This has eroded the country’s cost advantage, as manufacturing is positioned at low value-added segments of global value chains. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 117" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 117">ⓘ</button>
- [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd) joined the euro area in January 2026, replacing the longstanding currency board. This should reduce costs and strengthen integration, but a temporary increase in inflation from price resets is a risk. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses the OECD Economic Outlook projections for growth and unemployment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 10" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 10">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) Economic Outlook database projections for real GDP growth, unemployment, and inflation to assess growth momentum and potential output. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 23" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 23">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses the OECD Economic Outlook database for growth projections and historical data. Potential GDP growth is estimated to decline from over 4% in 2024 to 0.3% in 2070 due to demographic headwinds. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 89" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 89">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses its Economic Outlook Database for short-term projections (2025-2026) and the [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) Long-Term Model for medium- and long-term simulations (up to 2050). The long-term model incorporates scenarios for employment reforms, population growth, and fiscal consolidation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses simulations to estimate that structural reforms could raise potential GDP per capita growth by about 0.8 percentage points per year until 2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that labor productivity has stagnated at low levels over much of the past decade, partly reflecting a collapse in investment during the economic crisis. Real GDP growth has been weak during the last two decades, with negative contributions from labor productivity and employment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that Greece’s GDP-per-capita growth has outpaced the euro area since early 2021, marking a strong rebound from previous crises. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- Competitiveness gains have been achieved largely on the back of declining real wages. The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) warns that these gains may be lost if wages grow in excess of productivity. Unit labor costs have been increasing, though less so than in other [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) countries. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses potential GDP growth estimates to assess structural growth trends. It projects potential growth at 2.2–2.3% for 2024–2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 24" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 24">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD notes that weak private investment, innovation, and a shrinking working-age population continue to weigh on potential economic growth. Implementing structural reforms could raise GDP per capita growth by about 1.1 percentage points per year until 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- Rising wages have led to a strong increase in unit labor costs, weighing on the competitiveness of domestic firms. The working-age population is projected to further decline by 6% between 2024 and 2030. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 18">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) projects real GDP growth to remain modest at 0.4% in 2026 and 0.6% in 2027, weighed down by a surge in energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty. This follows moderate growth of 0.5% in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 13">ⓘ</button>
- Labour productivity growth has lagged the euro-area average since the mid-1990s. The level of multi-factor productivity declined between 2000 and 2022. The large share of small, low-productivity firms weighs on aggregate performance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 112" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses its Long-Term Model to project potential growth, accounting for policy reforms. It estimates that reforms in institutional quality, labor force participation, and R&D could raise GDP by 3.9% over 10 years and 11.9% over 25 years relative to baseline. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD projects robust real GDP growth of 3.7% in 2025 and 3.5% in 2026, driven by subsiding volatility from the multinational sector, improving financial conditions, and recovering exports <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 19" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 19">ⓘ</button>. Modified domestic demand, which excludes volatile multinational transactions, is projected to stabilize around 3.0% in 2025-26, below its long-term average of roughly 3.5% <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 19" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 19">ⓘ</button>.
- Assessing Irish GDP performance is complicated by multinational firms whose large transactions heavily impact national accounts, such as the sharp contraction in real GDP in 2023 due to reduced contract manufacturing, contrasting with a 5% increase in Modified Gross National Income (GNI*) <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17">ⓘ</button>.
- Downside risks to growth have risen, including geopolitical fragmentation, weaker global demand, tighter capacity constraints, and renewed pressures on energy and food prices <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 12" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 12">ⓘ</button>. Potential shocks to systemically important large firms could adversely impact the domestic economy and tax revenues <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>.
- The OECD uses Modified Domestic Demand (MDD) and Modified Gross National Income (GNI*) to capture underlying domestic dynamics, excluding volatile multinational transactions such as on-shored intellectual property and aircraft leasing <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17">ⓘ</button>.
- The OECD projects GDP growth to rebound to 3.1% in 2025 and 2.8% in 2026, significantly above the potential growth rates of 3.0% and 2.6% respectively, indicating a closing of the negative output gap from 2023 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28">ⓘ</button>.
- Strong wage growth has eroded cost competitiveness. Relative unit labour costs in the tradable sector have increased significantly since 2019. While still lower than in Germany, the differential has narrowed from 40% pre-pandemic to 20% in mid-2024 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 25">ⓘ</button>.
- Exports of goods declined in 2023, partly due to deteriorating competitiveness, particularly in agricultural and chemical products <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 26" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 26">ⓘ</button>.
- The OECD uses historical GDP growth data and projections for 2025–2026. It notes that potential GDP growth is expected to decline due to slower labour and productivity growth <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28">ⓘ</button>.
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses macroeconomic projections to assess growth trends, noting the impact of fiscal expansion and external uncertainty on GDP growth rates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses OECD Economic Outlook projections for real GDP growth, distinguishing between historical data and forecasts for 2025-2027. It also discusses potential GDP growth and the output gap, noting that the output gap is almost closed, supporting the case for fiscal consolidation <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34">ⓘ</button>.
- The OECD employs long-term modeling to estimate the impact of demographic changes and structural reforms on potential GDP growth. It projects that ageing could reduce the employment share of the population by 4 percentage points over 2025-2060 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 31">ⓘ</button>.

## Institutions and Data Sources

- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provides data on gross domestic product, inflation, population, and employment statistics cited in the reports. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 21" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 21">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the Country Reports and assessed the economic outlook. It provides economic forecasts, such as the Spring 2026 Forecast, used for growth and inflation projections. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: Conducted investment surveys highlighting obstacles such as skilled labour shortages and energy costs, which affect growth prospects. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 46, p. 103" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 46, p. 103">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provides data on gross domestic product, inflation, unemployment, and social statistics. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provides data on gross domestic product, inflation, tax revenues, debt, and structural indicators. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 43" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 43">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: Conducted investment surveys reporting on investment obstacles and access to finance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 12, p. 56" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 12, p. 56">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Bank’s Investment Survey is cited regarding obstacles to business investment in France, such as uncertainty, lack of skilled staff, and energy costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 65" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 65">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provides data on gross domestic product, investment, employment, unemployment, debt, and other economic indicators used throughout the report. It is the source for the investment gap graph and regional indicators. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 36-37, p. 118-119" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 36-37, p. 118-119">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: Referenced in the context of selected issues reports on Italy, particularly regarding drivers of firm-level productivity growth and business dynamism. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 58, p. 62, p. 63" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 58, p. 62, p. 63">ⓘ</button>
- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The report cites OECD data and assessments on better regulation practices, tax wedges, and productivity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 35, p. 59" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 35, p. 59">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The 2025 Investment Survey indicates that 71% of firms cited skilled staff availability as a long-term barrier to investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Cited as the source for national accounts data, labor force statistics, and taxation trends. Data on GDP growth, employment, and tax revenues are attributed to Eurostat datasets. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 3, 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 3, 42">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: Cited in the context of financial stability, investment surveys, and financial sector indicators. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 14, 63" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 14, 63">ⓘ</button>
- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: Referenced for assessments on productivity, regulatory burdens, and public finance reviews. The OECD’s Product Market Regulation indicators and economic surveys are used to benchmark Luxembourg's competitiveness and administrative barriers. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 14, 53" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 14, 53">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: Cited for data on firm access to finance, late payments surveys, and investment needs in circular economy and infrastructure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 13, 54, 78" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 13, 54, 78">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission issued the Country Report and the accompanying Recommendation for a Council Recommendation. It conducted an in-depth review of the Dutch economy under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure. The Commission also assessed the implementation of Country-Specific Recommendations and monitored the Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 30" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the Country Report and Spring 2026 Forecast. Assessed the implementation of country-specific recommendations (CSRs). Proposed abrogation of the excessive deficit procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Adopted recommendations on [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd)'s economic policies and the maximum growth rates of net expenditure. Endorsed the medium-term fiscal structural plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 29, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 29, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided statistical data on GDP, inflation, employment, debt, and other indicators cited in the report. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 9, p. 35, p. 38" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 9, p. 35, p. 38">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issuer of the Country Report and Country-Specific Recommendations (CSRs). Assesses progress on CSRs, monitors RRF implementation, and provides economic forecasts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 1-139" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 1-139">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Endorsed [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd)'s medium-term fiscal-structural plan and activated the national escape clause for defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 34, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 34, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: Referenced regarding investment surveys and data on business investment obstacles. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 56-59, p. 103" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 56-59, p. 103">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd)**: Mentioned in the context of backstop eligibility and institutional framework, though no direct support is cited in this specific report period beyond general eligibility assessments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 1" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 1">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: Referenced in the context of banking sector data, capital markets, and debt securities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 67-72" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 67-72">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurogroup](../institutions/eurogroup.qmd)**: Referenced indirectly via EU-level fiscal coordination and the national escape clause mechanism. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the country report and spring 2026 economic forecast. Assessed the implementation of country-specific recommendations and provided technical support for structural reforms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Activated the 'national escape clause' for Slovenia to allow higher defense spending in 2025. Endorsed Slovenia’s medium-term fiscal-structural plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: Target for inflation is 2%. The ECB’s medium-term target is referenced for inflation context. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided data on labor market, inflation, and structural indicators. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 21, p. 45" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 21, p. 45">ⓘ</button>
- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: Provided data on productivity, taxation, and regulatory barriers. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 13, p. 45, p. 54" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 13, p. 45, p. 54">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: Provided projections on aging-related expenditure and pension reform impacts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The issuer of the report, providing economic forecasts and assessments of Slovakia’s economic and fiscal policies. It issued Country-Specific Recommendations (CSRs) and monitored the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Adopted recommendations on Slovakia’s fiscal-structural plan and activated the National Escape Clause for defence spending. It also managed the Excessive Deficit Procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided statistical data on GDP, unemployment, inflation, and other indicators used in the report. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 22, p. 32" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 22, p. 32">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided data on general government deficit, debt, and defence expenditure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the recommendation. Provided the Spring 2026 Forecast projections for GDP, inflation, deficit, and debt. Assessed effective action for the excessive deficit procedure. Adopted the 2026 Alert Mechanism Report. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 3, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 3, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provides statistical data on GDP, inflation, unemployment, debt, and regional indicators used throughout the report. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35, p. 129" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35, p. 129">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the Country Report and Country-Specific Recommendations (CSRs) for 2025, focusing on fiscal sustainability, regulatory simplification, and social policies. It monitors Spain’s compliance with the EU fiscal framework and assesses the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 31">ⓘ</button>

- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Bank is cited in the context of surveying business constraints. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 86" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 86">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The International Monetary Fund is referenced regarding financial soundness indicators and stress tests. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Eurostat data is used for life expectancy, healthy life years, and unit labor cost comparisons. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd)'s MTFSP aligns with commitments under the revised EU fiscal rules approved by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd). Revisions to the NRRP milestones were agreed with the Commission in late 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: Data from the [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) is cited for Financial Soundness Indicators regarding banking system vulnerabilities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- **[World Bank](../institutions/world-bank.qmd)**: Corruption perceptions and governance indicators are sourced from the [World Bank](../institutions/world-bank.qmd) Worldwide Governance Indicators. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 46">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The [European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd) is mentioned in the context of public guarantee schemes and investment surveys. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 127" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 127">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The survey references the European Commission’s Ageing Report for economic and budgetary projections for EU Member States from 2022 to 2070 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 25">ⓘ</button>. It also cites the European Commission’s assessment of the draft Updated National Energy and Climate Plan of Ireland <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61">ⓘ</button>.
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The survey cites International Monetary Fund Article IV consultations and selected issues reports regarding Ireland, particularly concerning financial stability risks and non-bank financial institutions <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The OECD cites the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s 2024 Ageing Report for projections of ageing-related expenditure, which indicate a significant increase between 2022 and 2070 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 13">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)'s 2026 Draft Budgetary Plan as at risk of non-compliance with the EU fiscal framework but noted that deviations were within allowed flexibility margins. The Commission also confirmed the implementation status of the [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)n Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) implemented a policy rate cut in June 2025, leading to decreasing interest rates on loans and deposits in [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd). The Bank of Slovenia (national central bank) adjusted macroprudential tools, such as increasing the countercyclical capital buffer. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) is cited regarding the assessment of active labour market policies and the fiscal impact of pension reforms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 21" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 21">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The document references the EU Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) funds, which have supported investment and growth. The European Commission has endorsed Spain’s medium-term fiscal plan. The document also notes the alignment of national fiscal rules with the new EU fiscal framework overseen by the Commission <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 45" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 45">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The Bank of Spain has introduced a countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) of 0.5%, increasing to 1%, aligning with European Central Bank guidance on climate risk and financial stability. The ECB’s projections on the impact of RRP funds on potential growth are cited <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 35">ⓘ</button>.
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The document cites IMF stress tests indicating the banking sector is well-positioned to withstand shocks. It also references IMF Article IV consultations regarding fiscal policy and environmental taxation <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34, p. 51" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34, p. 51">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The document mentions the European Investment Bank’s role in supporting infrastructure and green transition projects, although specific financial flows are not detailed in the extracted figures <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30">ⓘ</button>.
- **[World Bank](../institutions/world-bank.qmd)**: The World Bank’s Worldwide Governance Indicators are cited in the context of corruption and public procurement challenges in Spain <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 54">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission notified a reversal of a milestone in April 2024 regarding the approval of national expenditure ceilings under the EU Recovery and Resilience Plan. The Commission also issued Country-Specific Recommendations in 2025, highlighting weaknesses in investment planning and transparency <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Bank (EIB) Investment Survey data are cited to show that lack of skilled staff is a pressing obstacle for investment in Slovakia. The EIB also notes that few companies report financing constraints as a major obstacle to investment <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 82, 90" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 82, 90">ⓘ</button>.
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) conducted stress tests in 2024, concluding that the Slovak banking sector possesses strong capacity to absorb shocks. The IMF’s Article IV Consultation Staff Report is also cited regarding pension reforms <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 25, 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 25, 30">ⓘ</button>.
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Eurostat data are used to track AI adoption among enterprises, showing that 18% of Slovak enterprises used AI in 2025. Eurostat also provides data on energy prices and electricity trading <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 109, 134, 137" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 109, 134, 137">ⓘ</button>.
